name: movie.title
why: Names the film for slates, filenames and the optional title card.

name: movie.logline
why: One sentence the resolver falls back on when a scene gives no description.

name: movie.fps
why: Fixes the frame clock every duration, ease and fx interval is quantised against.

name: movie.canvas
why: Delivery resolution, separate from aspect and from the oversized render frame.

name: movie.aspect
why: Framing decision independent of pixel canvas that drives every composition default.

name: movie.checkpoint
why: The image model is the true source of house style and must be overridable per chapter.

name: movie.lora_stack
why: Style and character LoRAs reach looks the base checkpoint cannot.
fallback: Missing LoRAs are skipped with a warning; tags carry the style instead.

name: movie.seed_root
why: One root seed makes a whole film reproducible and derives every per-shot seed.

name: movie.negative
default: [worst quality, low quality, bad anatomy, extra digits, watermark, text]
why: A global negative floor so no author has to remember the boilerplate.

name: movie.tag_style
why: Decides whether resolved variables emit tags or prose, changing every prompt builder.

name: movie.prompt_budget
why: Caps prompt length so late variables cannot silently push out character tags.

name: movie.prompt_priority
why: Decides what survives truncation when the prompt budget is hit.

name: movie.runtime_target_s
why: Lets the resolver warn or auto-trim when the cut overruns intended length.
fallback: Advisory lint only; never trims automatically.

name: movie.language
type: enum: en | ja | zh | ko | es | fr | de | other
why: Sets TTS voice pools, caption font and on-screen signage language at once.

name: movie.rating
why: Auto-populates the negative prompt and gates violence, gore and nudity tags.
fallback: Negative-prompt additions only; no post-render classifier.

name: movie.lint
why: Author-time warnings for crossed axis lines, impossible lens pairs and audio overruns.
fallback: Only checks needing no image analysis run; the rest are skipped silently.

name: movie.credits
why: Credit text is structural furniture the end chapter should build itself.
fallback: Rendered through the burnt-in caption engine over black; no scrolling crawl.

name: story.type
type: enum: short | episode | feature | music_video | trailer | pv | loop | anthology
why: Sets structural expectations, default scene lengths and whether an ending is required.

name: story.structure
type: enum: kishotenketsu | three_act | four_act | vignette | loop | anthology | freeform
why: Gives chapters default dramatic roles so pacing and music arcs can be derived.

name: story.chapter_role
type: enum: cold_open | ki | sho | ten | ketsu | act1 | act2 | act3 | interlude | epilogue | credits
why: One word tells pacing, music and grade what this chapter is for.

name: story.genre
type: enum: slice_of_life | drama | romance | comedy | action | thriller | horror | mystery | fantasy | sci_fi | mecha | sports | isekai | historical | supernatural | documentary
why: Seeds defaults for pace, lens, grade, music and sound across the film.

name: story.tone
type: enum: earnest | wistful | melancholy | tender | tense | dread | playful | comedic | absurd | cold | bittersweet | triumphant | eerie | serene | savage
why: The single tonality word every department reads when nothing more specific is set.

name: story.register
type: enum: naturalistic | heightened | stylised | melodrama | comedic_broad | poetic | clinical | mythic
why: How big performance, camera and music may be, separate from what they express.

name: story.tonality_curve
type: enum: flat | rising | falling | arc | inverted_arc | bittersweet | whiplash | spiral
why: States how tone moves across a chapter so grade, music and pace can interpolate.
fallback: Interpolates story.tension and audio.music.intensity per scene; no narrative reasoning.

name: story.mood
type: enum: neutral | warm | hopeful | lonely | anxious | grieving | angry | euphoric | numb | nostalgic | ominous | intimate | chaotic
why: Scene-level emotional colour biasing tags, grade, music and lighting together.

name: story.mood_intensity
why: Separates faint unease from panic without changing the mood word.

name: story.tension
why: One dial cut rate, music intensity, shake and contrast can all key off.

name: story.beat
type: enum: setup | inciting | rising | complication | turn | climax | falling | resolution | button | breather
why: Dramatic function of the scene, driving shot-size and pacing defaults.

name: story.scene_goal
why: One line of intent the prompt builder mines when a shot has no description.

name: story.pov
type: enum: objective | subjective | first_person | omniscient | unreliable | shared
why: Decides whose experience the camera, sound and grade are aligned to.

name: story.pov_char
why: Names whose eyeline, hearing perspective and emotional grade the scene follows.

name: story.reality_layer
type: enum: real | dream | memory | flashback | hallucination | imagined | story_within | digital | afterlife
why: Non-real layers need a consistent visual and audio treatment applied automatically.

name: story.time_position
type: enum: linear | earlier | later | parallel | timeless | recurring
why: Tells the viewer-facing devices (cards, grade shifts, reprise) when we are.

name: story.narrator
type: enum: none | char_vo | omniscient_vo | text_card | diary | letter
why: Declares that voice-over exists so the mix reserves headroom for it.

name: story.motif
why: Ties a recurring image, colour and musical phrase together under one name.
fallback: Injects the motif's tags and biases audio.music.motif; no automatic recall logic.

name: story.theme_tags
why: Thematic words that quietly bias imagery when a shot is under-specified.
fallback: Appended at low weight to the prompt tail; may be truncated by the budget.

name: story.title_card
type: enum: none | main_title | chapter_title | location_card | time_card | end_card
why: Cards are structural furniture and should not require a hand-built shot.
fallback: Burnt-in text frame over black or the shot; no animated typography.

name: story.content_flags
type: list of enum: violence | blood | death | injury | flashing_lights | body_horror | drowning | sexual_content | substance_use
why: Drives content warnings and softens flash and strobe fx automatically.

name: time.shot_s
why: Clip length; every camera ease, fx keyframe and audio cue depends on it.

name: time.scene_s
why: The scene-length control, usable as a budget shots are fitted into.
fallback: When shots overrun, the resolver warns and trims the last shot rather than re-editing.

name: time.chapter_s
why: Chapter budget so a film can be shaped to a runtime from the top down.
fallback: Advisory; overruns warn only.

name: time.fit_mode
type: enum: free | fit_to_budget | stretch_to_budget | trim_tail | drop_lowest_priority
why: Says what happens when authored shots do not add up to the declared scene length.
fallback: Only free and trim_tail are implemented; others warn and behave as free.

name: time.pace
type: enum: languid | slow | steady | brisk | fast | frantic
why: One inheritable word setting default shot lengths and cut rate for a sequence.

name: time.cut_rate
why: Numeric handle on editing density when the pace word is too coarse.
fallback: Picks default shot durations at author time; no automatic re-cutting.

name: time.rhythm
type: enum: even | accelerating | decelerating | syncopated | stuttered | long_short | breathing
why: Shot-length pattern is what makes an edit feel composed rather than uniform.
fallback: Applied as a multiplier curve over default shot durations.

name: time.min_shot_s
why: Floor that stops generated pacing producing unreadable flash cuts.

name: time.max_shot_s
why: Ceiling keeping a single LTX chain from drifting beyond usable coherence.

name: time.hold_in_s
why: A held beat before motion starts makes a cut land instead of lurching.

name: time.hold_out_s
why: Settling before the cut makes the outgoing frame feel composed.

name: time.clip_chain
why: Makes the renderer's chaining explicit so long shots are authored knowingly.
fallback: Chained clips joined with a short crossfade; drift accumulates past ~3 links.

name: time.chain_overlap_frames
why: Overlap between chained clips is the main lever on how visible a join is.
fallback: Implemented as a crossfade of that length; no latent-space continuity.

name: time.speed
why: Straight retime of the rendered clip, the cheapest slow-motion available.

name: time.speed_ramp
type: enum: none | ramp_down | ramp_up | freeze_then_go | slowmo_hit | stutter | ramp_in_out
why: Time manipulation is core anime action grammar and needs a first-class name.

name: time.freeze_at_pct
why: Where a freeze lands is the whole joke or the whole impact.

name: time.freeze_hold_s
why: How long a freeze holds separates a stutter from a title beat.

name: time.beat_grid
type: enum: free | music_beat | music_bar | music_phrase | metronome
why: Lets cuts snap to the generated music instead of floating against it.
fallback: Cuts stay on authored times; the resolver reports nearest musical grid offsets.

name: time.sync_to_music
why: Marks the individual shots that must land on a musical hit.
fallback: Ignored; shot uses its authored duration.

name: time.pre_roll_s
why: Silent lead-in before the first shot for breathing room after a transition.

name: time.post_roll_s
why: Tail after the last shot so a scene can end on held air.

name: shot.purpose
type: enum: establish | reveal | react | action | dialogue | transition | detail | beat | mood | insert
why: One word from which size, move, lens, duration and audio defaults derive.

name: shot.size
type: enum: extreme_close_up | close_up | medium_close_up | medium | medium_wide | wide | extreme_wide | insert | macro | establishing
why: The most-used image decision; without it every keyframe is a random crop.

name: shot.framing_type
type: enum: single | two_shot | three_shot | group | over_shoulder | pov | reaction | insert_object | empty_frame | crowd
why: How many bodies are in frame and from whose vantage, changing the whole tag stack.

name: shot.subject
type: list of char.id or object id
why: Names who the shot is about so face refs and focus target the right body.

name: shot.action
why: Free-text beat description filling any gap the structured variables leave.

name: shot.tags
type: list of tags (appends down the hierarchy)
why: The escape hatch that keeps the format from blocking a prompt the model can do.

name: shot.negative_add
why: Scoped negatives so one artefact dies without touching the global list.

name: shot.seed
why: Deterministic per-shot noise and the handle for re-rolling exactly one frame.

name: shot.cfg
why: Prompt adherence versus image quality, the main generation trade-off.

name: shot.steps
why: Quality/time trade so hero shots can cost more than filler.

name: shot.keyframe_mode
why: Controls whether the shot is single-image i2v or interpolation between authored frames.
fallback: Collapses to start_only plus a post camera move when end-frame conditioning is unavailable.

name: shot.motion_strength
why: How much the video model may move the frame, the main coherence dial.

name: shot.motion_prompt
why: The text the i2v pass sees, a different sentence from the keyframe prompt.

name: shot.still
why: A held drawing with no video pass is legitimate anime and saves render time.

name: shot.hero
why: Marks shots worth extra steps, upscaling and retries without setting each by hand.

name: shot.retries
why: How many times a failed or rejected generation is re-rolled before giving up.

name: shot.priority
why: Tells budget allocators and trimmers which shots to sacrifice first.

name: shot.match_prev
type: enum: none | match_frame | match_action | match_graphic | match_eyeline | match_light
why: Asks for a cut landing on the previous composition instead of hand-copying values.
fallback: Copies the previous shot's framing variables at author time; no image-space alignment.

name: shot.reference
why: A reference image is often faster and more reliable than any number of tags.
fallback: Face references work via IPAdapter; background and lighting references warn and are ignored.

name: shot.reference_weight
why: How hard the reference pulls against the prompt, per shot.

name: shot.facing
type: enum: to_camera | three_quarter_left | three_quarter_right | profile_left | profile_right | back_three_quarter | back
why: Body orientation is a separate axis from camera angle and the main read on a character.

name: shot.cam.height
type: enum: ground | ankle | knee | waist | chest | eye | high | overhead | aerial
why: Camera height reads as power and scale, authored independently of tilt.

name: shot.cam.angle
type: enum: level | low | high | birds_eye | worms_eye | top_down | dutch
why: Tilt relative to the subject is the classic dominance lever.

name: shot.cam.dutch_deg
why: Continuous amount for the dutch angle instead of a binary on/off.
fallback: Rounded into a dutch-angle keyframe tag; no post rotation pass.

name: shot.cam.move
type: enum: static | push | pull | pan_l | pan_r | tilt_u | tilt_d | handheld | zoom_in | zoom_out | dolly_l | dolly_r | crane_up | crane_down | orbit_l | orbit_r | whip_pan | roll | rack_zoom | follow
why: The core motion verb, extending eight native moves to what directors ask for.
fallback: First eight render natively; dolly maps to pan, crane to tilt+push, orbit to pan+push, roll and rack_zoom to push with a warning.

name: shot.cam.move_speed
type: enum: still | crawl | slow | medium | fast | whip
why: Separates how fast from what direction so one move serves whisper and chase.

name: shot.cam.move_amount
why: Speed alone cannot distinguish a 3% breathing push from a 40% lunge.

name: shot.cam.move_ease
type: enum: linear | ease_in | ease_out | ease_in_out | snap | overshoot | settle
why: Linear moves are the tell of machine-made footage; easing feels operated.
fallback: Built from zoompan/crop expressions; snap and overshoot degrade to ease_in_out.

name: shot.cam.move_start_pct
why: Lets a move begin after a held beat instead of always on the cut.
fallback: Quantised to a hold-then-move two-segment filter chain.

name: shot.cam.move_end_pct
why: Lets a move settle before the cut.
fallback: Quantised to a move-then-hold two-segment filter chain.

name: shot.cam.move_anchor
type: enum: center | face | subject | thirds_l | thirds_r | horizon | custom_xy
why: A push to frame centre and a push to a character's eye are different shots.
fallback: face/subject resolve to a fixed x/y offset chosen at author time, not tracked.

name: shot.cam.rig
type: enum: locked | tripod | handheld_light | handheld_heavy | shoulder | steadicam | gimbal | drone | crane | dolly_track
why: Baseline motion texture for a sequence so every shot needn't set shake.
fallback: Maps to handheld amplitude/frequency presets; drone and crane borrow push/tilt.

name: shot.cam.shake_amp
why: Explicit instability for impacts and panic without changing the move type.

name: shot.cam.shake_freq
type: enum: slow_drift | breath | walk | run | impact | rumble
why: Amplitude without frequency gives every shake the same character.
fallback: Mapped onto shake fx presets; uncommon frequencies snap to the nearest.

name: shot.cam.zoom_kind
why: Documents that post zooms crop resolution, which is why overscan matters.

name: shot.cam.subject_distance_m
why: Ties focal length and shot size together so the pair stays coherent.
fallback: Advisory only; used to lint lens against size, never sent to the renderer.

name: shot.cam.shutter_angle
why: How crisp or smeared motion reads, the difference between a war film and a dream.
fallback: Buckets into smear fx amount; 45 renders as none, 360 as heavy.

name: shot.cam.motion_blur
why: Direct override when shutter angle is too indirect for the author.
fallback: Drives smear fx strength only; LTX supplies whatever native blur it produces.

name: shot.cam.rolling_shutter
why: Skew on fast pans is a specific found-footage signature some films want.
fallback: Ignored.

name: shot.lens.look
type: enum: ultra_wide | wide | normal | portrait | tele | super_tele | fisheye | anamorphic | macro
why: Lets an author state the feel without knowing millimetres; this maps to tags.
fallback: Prompt-tag approximation on the keyframe; no lens simulation.

name: shot.lens.focal_mm
why: A number authors think in, from which compression and dof defaults derive.
fallback: Bucketed into wide/tele/fisheye tags; no true optical geometry.

name: shot.lens.compression
why: How flat the background stacks when focal length alone doesn't sell it.
fallback: Expressed as background-scale and perspective tags only.

name: shot.lens.distortion
type: enum: none | mild_barrel | strong_barrel | fisheye | pincushion
why: Wide-angle bulge is a deliberate anime device for panic and comedy.
fallback: Baked as a fisheye/distortion tag; no post-warp pass.

name: shot.lens.flare
type: enum: none | subtle | anamorphic_streak | warm_bloom | starburst | veiling
why: Flare is a mood signature authors reach for constantly.
fallback: A lens-flare tag plus the glow fx; not a positioned, moving flare.

name: shot.lens.bokeh_shape
type: enum: circular | hexagonal | oval_anamorphic | swirly | cats_eye | bloom_blobs
why: Out-of-focus highlight shape is much of a night film's identity.
fallback: Generic bokeh tag; shape ignored.

name: shot.lens.filtration
type: enum: none | light_diffusion | pro_mist | heavy_diffusion | glimmer | smoke_glass
why: Diffusion is the cheapest way to unify a look across shots and should inherit.
fallback: Approximated by glow fx strength plus soft-light tags.

name: shot.lens.vignette
why: Corner falloff quietly focuses attention and is expected in cinematic grades.
fallback: Global gamma pull plus a vignetting tag; no radial mask.

name: shot.lens.breathing
why: Focus pulls that change framing are a realism cue for handheld passages.
fallback: Ignored; framing stays locked.

name: shot.focus.dof
type: enum: deep | medium | shallow | very_shallow | split_diopter
why: How much of the world is sharp is the fastest character/background separation.
fallback: Prompt tags only; no aperture simulation.

name: shot.focus.point
type: enum: eyes | face | subject | hands | prop | foreground | midground | background | hyperfocal
why: Names what must be sharp so generator and blur pass agree on the subject.
fallback: Tags plus which layer receives blur; not a measured focal plane.

name: shot.focus.behavior
type: enum: locked | rack_to_bg | rack_to_fg | follow_subject | soft_throughout | snap_focus
why: A rack focus is a dramatic beat that currently cannot be authored at all.
fallback: Two keyframes joined by a short dissolve, or a single end-focus frame with a warning.

name: shot.focus.rack_at_pct
why: A rack that lands on a line of dialogue needs its timing authored.
fallback: Ignored; the substitute dissolve is centred.

name: shot.focus.bg_blur
why: Continuous background separation that survives even without true dof.
fallback: Keyframe tag strength; not a post blur on the moving clip.

name: shot.focus.fg_blur
why: Soft foreground occluders are the cheapest depth cue in the language.
fallback: Keyframe tag only; true plane blur needs the layer compositor.

name: shot.focus.softness
why: Global softness for flashbacks and dreams, independent of depth.
fallback: Approximated with glow fx; no separable diffusion filter.

name: shot.comp.eyeline
type: enum: into_lens | left | right | up | down | off_left | off_right | closed | at_object
why: Where a character looks carries the emotional read and stitches reverses together.

name: shot.comp.screen_direction
type: enum: l_to_r | r_to_l | to_camera | away_from_camera | static
why: Keeps travel and chase geometry consistent instead of flipping randomly.
fallback: Drives tags and mirror-flip of the keyframe; not geometrically enforced.

name: shot.comp.axis_line
why: Declares the 180-degree line so reverses can be checked rather than eyeballed.
fallback: Author-time lint warning only; render unchanged.

name: shot.comp.balance
type: enum: symmetrical | asym_left | asym_right | weighted_bottom | weighted_top | diagonal | radial | chaotic
why: Visual weight distribution is what an author means when a frame feels wrong.
fallback: Composition tags only; unverified.

name: shot.comp.negative_space
why: Emptiness is the loudest tool for loneliness and dread and needs a dial.
fallback: Biases shot.size and subject-scale tags.

name: shot.comp.subject_scale
why: Continuous control between the coarse steps of shot.size.
fallback: Rounded to the nearest shot.size tag.

name: shot.comp.thirds_bias
type: enum: center | left_third | right_third | golden_l | golden_r | symmetrical | edge_left | edge_right
why: Where the subject sits laterally is the composition choice authors most want.
fallback: Tag plus horizontal crop offset inside the overscan margin.

name: shot.comp.headroom
why: The most common framing error and the most common deliberate tension device.
fallback: Tags plus a small post crop nudge; not measured against the generated head.

name: shot.comp.lookroom
type: enum: auto | left | right | center | none
why: Space in front of a looking character makes a frame balanced or trapped.
fallback: Auto derives from eyeline and applies a crop offset; tags carry the rest.

name: shot.comp.horizon
type: enum: none | low | lower_third | center | upper_third | high
why: Horizon placement sets whether a character dominates sky or is crushed by ground.
fallback: Prompt tag plus vertical crop bias; unverified.

name: shot.comp.leading_lines
type: enum: none | one_point | diagonal | radial | vertical | horizontal | spiral | converging_rails
why: Directed lines tell the eye where to go and anime backgrounds lean on them.
fallback: Perspective and vanishing-point tags on the keyframe.

name: shot.comp.perspective
type: enum: flat | one_point | two_point | three_point | isometric | fisheye | overhead_map
why: Perspective construction is an explicit background-art decision in anime.
fallback: Perspective tags on the keyframe.

name: shot.comp.frame_in_frame
type: enum: none | doorway | window | mirror | foliage | crowd | curtain | tunnel | fence
why: Framing a character inside an in-world aperture compactly states confinement.

name: shot.comp.depth_stack
why: How many depth planes the frame is built from; the contract with layer variables.
fallback: Foreground-occluder tags; true separated planes need the layer renderer.

name: shot.frame.aspect_override
why: A single shot in a different ratio shouldn't restructure the chapter.

name: shot.frame.letterbox
type: enum: none | bars_2_39 | bars_2_1 | pillars_4_3 | dynamic_widen
why: Aspect change as a dramatic device needs to be authorable mid-film.

name: shot.frame.caption_safe
type: enum: bottom_10 | bottom_15 | bottom_20 | top | none
why: Reserves the zone burnt-in captions occupy so compositions survive delivery.

name: shot.fx
type: list of enum: punch | shake | aberr | glow | flash | hot | ramp | smear | whiteout
why: Direct access to the native fx set, appended down the hierarchy.

name: shot.fx_intensity
why: One strength dial so the same fx list can whisper or scream.

name: shot.fx_at_pct
why: Where in the shot each effect fires, the whole timing of an impact.

name: shot.fx.impact_frame
type: enum: none | white_flash | black_flash | negative | sketch_frame | silhouette_pop
why: The one-frame graphic hit is a defining anime action beat already supported.

name: shot.fx.speed_lines
type: enum: none | radial | horizontal | vertical | impact | motion_trail
why: Graphic motion overlays are native anime language with no photographic equivalent.

name: shot.fx.bg_treatment
type: enum: matched | watercolor | photobash | abstract_color | radial_burst | pattern | void_black | white_void | emotional_wash
why: Dropping the real background for an emotional field is standard anime grammar.

name: shot.fx.emote_symbols
type: list of enum: sweatdrop | vein_pop | blush_lines | shock_lines | sparkles | teardrop | steam | question_mark | chibi_pop
why: Anime's symbolic emotion vocabulary is a real expressive channel, not decoration.

name: shot.fx.screentone
type: enum: none | dots | hatch | gradient | flash_lines | mood_tone
why: Manga screentone as a mood device is a distinct look from film grain.
fallback: Requested as a keyframe tag; no composited tone plate.

name: edit.transition_in
type: enum: cut | dissolve | fade_black | fade_white | flash | whip_pan | wipe | iris | smash | match_cut
why: How this shot arrives, authored on the shot that owns the change.

name: edit.transition_out
type: enum: cut | dissolve | fade_black | fade_white | flash | whip_pan | wipe | iris | smash | hold
why: How this shot leaves, so a scene's last shot can fade without a phantom shot.

name: edit.transition_s
why: Transition length is the difference between a blink and a chapter break.

name: edit.transition_dir
type: enum: auto | left | right | up | down | in | out | radial
why: Wipes, irises and whip pans are meaningless without a direction.

name: edit.scene_transition
type: enum: cut | dissolve | fade_black | fade_white | iris | wipe | match_cut | smash | time_card
why: Scene boundaries deserve a stronger default than shot boundaries.

name: edit.chapter_transition
type: enum: cut | fade_black | fade_white | title_card | iris | long_dissolve
why: Chapter breaks are structural punctuation the audience must feel.

name: edit.cut_on_action
why: Cutting mid-movement hides the join between two independently generated clips.
fallback: Applied as a small trim of head/tail frames; no motion analysis.

name: edit.match_cut_target
why: A match cut needs to name the shape it is matching, not just request one.
fallback: Copies the target's composition variables into this shot; no image-space matching.

name: edit.audio_lead_s
why: Letting sound arrive before picture is the standard way to bind two shots.

name: edit.montage
type: enum: none | time_passing | training | travel | memory | investigation | ruin
why: Montage is a scene shape with its own pacing and music rules.
fallback: Sets pace, transitions and music defaults; shots still authored individually.

name: edit.insert_flash_frames
why: Subliminal single-frame inserts are a horror and memory device already renderable.

name: edit.repeat
why: Repeating a cut is how a loop, a stutter or an obsession is edited.

name: layer.count
why: Declares how many depth planes exist, the root of the whole layers feature.
fallback: Above 1 the planes are described in the prompt but rendered into one flat keyframe.

name: layer.mode
why: Says whether layers are only described or actually rendered and composited apart.
fallback: tag_hinted works today; masked and generated_separate degrade to it with a warning.

name: layer.bg.content
why: The background is most of the frame and should be authored once per scene.

name: layer.bg.render
type: enum: sketch | simple | detailed | ultra_detailed | painted_bg | photobash
why: Background finish level is a deliberate contrast tool against character line quality.

name: layer.bg.blur
why: Per-plane blur is what actually separates a character from the world.
fallback: Falls through to focus.bg_blur tags on the flat keyframe.

name: layer.bg.value
type: enum: darker | matched | lighter | washed | silhouette
why: Tonal separation between planes is how a frame reads at a glance.
fallback: Applied as a global grade bias when no plane separation exists.

name: layer.bg.motion
type: enum: static | drift | parallax_slow | parallax_fast | scroll_l | scroll_r
why: A moving background plane is the signature of the anime pan.
fallback: Renders as a single-plane push or pan on the flat keyframe.

name: layer.mid.content
why: The midground is where the set lives and where characters stand.

name: layer.mid.occupancy
why: How much midground clutter sits between camera and background.
fallback: Density tags only.

name: layer.fg.content
type: enum or string: none | foliage | railing | crowd | glass | curtain | doorframe | rain | dust | shoulder | hand | custom
why: A foreground occluder is the cheapest way to make a flat generation feel deep.

name: layer.fg.coverage
why: How much of the frame the occluder eats, from a hint to a near-total block.
fallback: Expressed as tag emphasis; not measured.

name: layer.fg.blur
why: Foreground elements read as foreground mainly because they are soft.
fallback: Keyframe tag only until the compositor exists.

name: layer.fg.motion
type: enum: static | sway | pass_through | drift | parallax
why: Something crossing the lens is the strongest depth cue in a moving clip.
fallback: Requested of LTX via the motion prompt; unreliable and unenforced.

name: layer.parallax_strength
why: How far the planes separate during a move, the whole point of 2.5D.
fallback: Ignored; the move applies uniformly to the flat frame.

name: layer.character_plane
why: Says which plane the subject occupies so blur and parallax treat them correctly.
fallback: Used only to decide which blur values apply to the subject tags.

name: layer.sky_plane
why: Sky as its own plane lets clouds move while the ground stays locked.
fallback: Sky renders inside the background plate.

name: layer.depth_map
why: An explicit depth pass is the prerequisite for real per-plane blur and parallax.
fallback: Not generated; all depth effects fall back to tags.

name: world.place
why: Where we are is the first thing a background prompt needs.

name: world.place_id
why: A named location lets every scene there share plates, light and ambience.

name: world.interior_exterior
type: enum: interior | exterior | threshold | vehicle | underground | underwater | aerial | void
why: Interior or exterior decides light motivation, reverb and weather visibility at once.

name: world.biome
type: enum: urban | suburb | rural | school | coastal | mountain | forest | desert | snowfield | industrial | transit | domestic | fantasy_realm | space | ruins
why: Coarse world class from which dressing, ambience and practicals are seeded.

name: world.era
type: enum: ancient | feudal | victorian | early_20c | showa | modern | near_future | far_future | post_apocalyptic | timeless
why: Period drives architecture, wardrobe, props and signage without per-shot tagging.

name: world.tech_level
type: enum: pre_industrial | industrial | electric | digital | networked | cyber | spacefaring | magitech
why: Separates technology from period so a fantasy world can carry modern devices.

name: world.season
type: enum: spring | early_summer | summer | late_summer | autumn | winter | rainy_season | dry_season
why: Season sets foliage, wardrobe, light angle and ambience in one word.

name: world.time_of_day
type: enum: pre_dawn | dawn | morning | midday | afternoon | golden_hour | dusk | blue_hour | night | deep_night
why: Time of day is the single strongest driver of colour temperature and mood.

name: world.clock_time
why: An exact hour lets sun angle and on-screen clocks agree across a scene.
fallback: Bucketed into world.time_of_day; no real sun solver.

name: world.weather
type: enum: clear | fair | overcast | rain | drizzle | downpour | thunderstorm | snow | blizzard | fog | mist | wind | heat_haze | sandstorm | ash | aurora
why: The weather variable the author asked for, seeding light, particles and ambience.

name: world.weather_intensity
why: Drizzle and downpour are the same word at different strengths.

name: world.precip_render
type: enum: none | tag_only | streaks | droplets_on_lens | splashes | drawn_lines | sheet_rain
why: How precipitation is actually drawn is a look decision separate from whether it falls.
fallback: Keyframe tags plus optional overlay noise; no simulated particle pass.

name: world.cloud_cover
why: Cloud cover decides shadow hardness even when weather is otherwise clear.

name: world.fog_density
why: Atmospheric depth is the cheapest way to separate planes in a painting.

name: world.wind_speed
type: enum: still | breeze | steady | gusty | strong | gale
why: Wind drives hair, cloth, foliage and particle motion prompts together.

name: world.wind_dir
type: enum: none | l_to_r | r_to_l | toward_camera | away | swirling | updraft
why: Wind without a direction makes every sway contradict the next shot.
fallback: Fed to the motion prompt and hair/cloth tags; not physically enforced.

name: world.ground_state
type: enum: dry | damp | wet_reflective | puddled | muddy | snow | ice | sand | grass | tatami | tile
why: Wet ground doubles the light in a night scene and must be stated, not implied.

name: world.air_particles
type: list of enum: none | dust | pollen | petals | ash | embers | snow | leaves | bubbles | fireflies | steam | spores
why: Drifting particles are the standard anime way to fill dead air in a frame.

name: world.crowd_density
type: enum: empty | sparse | moderate | busy | packed
why: How populated a place is changes composition, ambience and generation difficulty.

name: world.traffic
type: enum: none | occasional | steady | congested | rush
why: Vehicle presence drives background motion, ambience and passing-light cues.

name: world.set_dressing
why: Named props and furniture keep a location recognisable across shots.

name: world.signage_language
type: enum: inherit | ja | en | none | invented | blurred
why: On-screen text is a constant generation artefact and needs an explicit policy.
fallback: Non-inherit values become prompt and negative tags; legibility is not guaranteed.

name: world.scale_cue
type: enum: none | human_figure | vehicle | building | horizon | giant_object
why: Anime sells scale by putting a known object in frame, not by focal length.

name: world.sky_state
type: enum: auto | clear_blue | cirrus | cumulus | storm | sunset_gradient | starfield | moonlit | red_sky | no_sky
why: The sky is a designed graphic element in anime, not a byproduct of weather.

name: world.celestial
type: enum: none | sun_visible | moon_full | moon_crescent | stars | comet | eclipse | twin_moons
why: A visible sun or moon anchors direction, time and often the whole composition.

name: world.ambient_life
type: list of enum: none | cicadas | birds | crickets | frogs | wind_chimes | distant_traffic | school_noise | machinery | waves | river
why: Living background sound is what makes a location feel inhabited between lines.

name: world.smell_note
why: A sensory note the prompt builder can mine for haze, steam and colour cues.
fallback: Mined for tags only; contributes nothing when the prompt budget is tight.

name: char.present
why: Declares who exists in the scene so shots can default their subjects.

name: char.id
why: A stable handle every shot, line and face reference points at.

name: char.name
why: Display name for captions, credits and speaker labels.

name: char.role
type: enum: lead | deuteragonist | support | antagonist | foil | mentor | extra | crowd | narrator
why: Role decides prompt priority, face-weight budget and how often the character anchors a shot.

name: char.design_tags
why: The canonical appearance tag bundle re-injected into every prompt.

name: char.face_sheet
why: The IPAdapter sheet is the only real mechanism for face consistency today.

name: char.face_weight
why: How hard the face reference pulls against expression and angle.

name: char.face_weight_by_size
why: A face lock that helps a close-up wrecks a wide, so it must vary by shot size.
fallback: Applied as a fixed lookup table; no detection of actual face size in frame.

name: char.age_read
type: enum: child | preteen | teen | young_adult | adult | middle_aged | elderly | ageless
why: Apparent age is a tag-level decision that must never drift between shots.

name: char.build
type: enum: petite | slim | average | athletic | stocky | heavy | tall_lean | muscular
why: Body type is part of a silhouette and is otherwise re-rolled every generation.

name: char.height_cm
why: Relative height drives two-shot framing and eyeline geometry.
fallback: Used at author time to bias framing tags; not measured in the render.

name: char.hair
why: Hair is the primary recognition cue in anime and must be locked explicitly.

name: char.eyes
why: Eye colour and shape carry identity even when the face style changes.

name: char.skin
why: Skin tone drifts between generations unless it is restated each prompt.

name: char.distinguishing
why: Scars, moles, glasses and ahoge are the details that survive stylisation.

name: char.lora
why: A trained character LoRA outperforms any tag bundle when one exists.
fallback: Skipped with a warning if absent; design tags and the face sheet carry identity.

name: char.wear.outfit
why: The wardrobe variable, inheritable so a chapter can change clothes once.

name: char.wear.layer
type: list of enum: none | coat | jacket | scarf | hood | apron | armour | cloak | bag | umbrella
why: Outer layers change silhouette and are added or removed as dramatic action.

name: char.wear.state
type: enum: neat | casual | rumpled | soaked | dusty | bloodied | torn | burnt | half_dressed | formal
why: Costume condition is how a story's damage stays visible on screen.

name: char.wear.accessories
why: Small repeated objects are identity anchors and often motif carriers.

name: char.wear.colors
why: Costume colour must be locked or a character reads differently every scene.
fallback: Injected as colour tags; grade extremes can still shift them.

name: char.props_held
why: What is in a character's hands drives both framing and hand-drawing failures.

name: char.emotion
type: enum: neutral | happy | sad | angry | afraid | surprised | disgusted | contempt | tender | embarrassed | determined | exhausted | numb | anxious | relieved | joyful | grieving
why: The per-character emotion the author asked for, driving face, voice and pose together.

name: char.emotion_intensity
why: Anger at 0.2 and 0.9 are different performances, not different emotions.

name: char.emotion_secondary
type: enum: none | plus any char.emotion value
why: Real performance is usually two feelings at once and the mix is the acting.
fallback: Blended as a lower-weight expression tag and a softer TTS emotion vector.

name: char.emotion_mask
type: enum: none | suppressed | forced_smile | fake_calm | breaking | deadpan | performative
why: A character hiding a feeling is a distinct expression from having it.

name: char.expression
why: Direct override for when the derived expression is not the drawing wanted.

name: char.brow
type: enum: neutral | raised | furrowed | one_raised | flat | pleading | angry_v
why: Brows carry more of an anime face's read than the mouth does.

name: char.mouth
type: enum: closed | slight_open | open | wide_open | smile | smirk | frown | grimace | gritted | trembling | wavy
why: Mouth shape must be separable from dialogue so silent reactions can be authored.

name: char.blush
why: Blush is a first-class emotional signal in anime, not an incidental detail.

name: char.tears
type: enum: none | welling | single | streaming | wiped | dried_tracks | comedic_fountain
why: Crying has discrete drawn stages that a generic emotion word cannot select.

name: char.gaze_target
why: Naming who is looked at keeps eyelines consistent across a reverse.
fallback: Resolved into eyeline direction tags at author time; not geometrically verified.

name: char.posture
type: enum: standing | slouched | upright | leaning | sitting | seiza | crouched | kneeling | lying | curled | floating | falling
why: Posture states character before the face is even visible.

name: char.gesture
type: string or enum: none | pointing | reaching | covering_face | clenched_fists | hands_in_pockets | arms_crossed | waving | bowing | shielding | holding_out
why: Hands are where performance lives and where generation fails without direction.

name: char.energy
why: One dial for how much a body is doing, feeding motion strength and voice pace.

name: char.movement
type: enum: still | idle | walking | running | sprinting | turning | rising | sitting_down | falling | fighting | dancing | flying
why: What the body does is the core of the i2v motion prompt.

name: char.condition
type: enum: healthy | tired | injured | bleeding | ill | soaked | freezing | overheated | drunk | possessed
why: Physical state must persist across shots or continuity collapses.

name: char.arc_stage
type: enum: introduced | stable | pressured | breaking | changed | resolved | absent
why: Where a character sits in their arc biases wardrobe, grade and performance defaults.
fallback: Advisory bias on expression and colour defaults; no narrative enforcement.

name: char.relationship
why: Blocking distance, eyelines and voice register all follow from who these people are to each other.
fallback: Used to pick blocking and framing defaults at author time only.

name: block.pattern
type: enum: static | approach | retreat | circle | side_by_side | face_off | pass_by | cross | gather | scatter | follow
why: The blocking variable, describing how bodies move relative to each other.
fallback: Drives per-shot framing and motion-prompt defaults; no staging simulation.

name: block.positions
why: Who stands where in frame is what makes reverses and group shots readable.
fallback: Becomes left/right/centre composition tags; exact placement is unverified.

name: block.distance
type: enum: intimate | personal | social | public | distant
why: Proxemics is the fastest read on a relationship and needs its own word.

name: block.orientation
type: enum: facing | angled | side_by_side | back_to_back | one_turned_away | over_shoulder
why: How two bodies face each other is a separate axis from where they stand.

name: block.contact
type: enum: none | near_touch | hand_touch | hand_hold | embrace | grab | strike | carry | lean_on
why: Physical contact is the hardest thing to generate and must be explicitly asked for.
fallback: Contact tags plus a lower motion strength; anatomy failures are common and retried.

name: block.entrance
type: enum: none | walks_in_l | walks_in_r | enters_bg | rises_into | reveal_by_pan | already_present
why: How a character arrives in frame is a directing choice, not an accident of generation.
fallback: Requested via the motion prompt or staged as a camera move; not guaranteed.

name: block.exit
type: enum: none | walks_out_l | walks_out_r | exits_bg | drops_out | left_behind
why: Exits punctuate scenes and decide whether the next shot needs the character at all.
fallback: Motion-prompt hint plus cut timing; not guaranteed.

name: block.group_shape
type: enum: line | wedge | cluster | circle | scattered | tiered | isolated_one
why: Group compositions fail without a stated shape and become tag soup.
fallback: Composition tags only; crowd arrangement is whatever the model produces.

name: light.motivation
type: enum: sun | moon | sky_ambient | practical | firelight | screen_glow | neon | fluorescent | streetlamp | headlights | magic | bioluminescence | unmotivated | mixed
why: One scene-level answer to where light comes from, seeding direction, colour and quality.

name: light.key_dir
type: enum: front | front_l | front_r | side_l | side_r | back_l | back_r | back | top | bottom | ambient_none
why: Key direction is the primary shape of a face and must be shot-addressable.

name: light.key_elev
type: enum: below | eye | above | steep_above | overhead
why: Underlighting versus toplighting reads as horror versus grace.

name: light.quality
type: enum: hard | medium | soft | very_soft | overcast_flat | specular_wet
default: auto (hard for sun, very_soft for overcast)
why: Shadow edge hardness sets the emotional temperature of a whole location.

name: light.ratio
type: enum: flat_1_1 | low_2_1 | normal_4_1 | dramatic_8_1 | chiaroscuro_16_1 | silhouette
why: Key-to-fill ratio is the numeric handle on drama.
fallback: Tag stack plus a curves/eq contrast bump; not a measured ratio.

name: light.fill
type: enum: none | bounce | soft_fill | negative_fill | ambient_sky
why: Explicit fill separates a moody frame from a muddy one.
fallback: Tags plus shadow lift in the grade.

name: light.rim
type: enum: none | subtle | strong | halo | kiss | double_rim
why: Rim light is the defining separation device of anime and should be on by default.

name: light.rim_color
why: A coloured rim ties a character to the location's neon, fire or moonlight.
fallback: Named colours become tags; arbitrary hex snaps to the nearest name.

name: light.practicals
type: list of enum: neon_sign | desk_lamp | ceiling_fluoro | candle | fireplace | monitor | phone_screen | streetlight | lantern | headlights | moon_window | stage_light | vending_machine
why: In-frame sources declared once keep every shot agreeing where glow comes from.

name: light.shadow_gobo
type: enum: none | blinds | foliage | branches | grate | curtain | crowd | rain_streaks | water_caustics | window_cross
why: Patterned shadow is the highest-value-per-token lighting device in tag space.

name: light.shadow_density
why: How black the blacks go, separate from overall contrast.
fallback: Curves shadow crush plus tags.

name: light.temp_k
why: Colour temperature is the most reliable time-of-day and interior signal.

name: light.contrast_scheme
type: enum: neutral | warm_key_cool_fill | cool_key_warm_rim | teal_orange | magenta_cyan | sodium_night | monochrome_wash | candle_vs_moon
why: Colour contrast between key and fill gives depth without extra lights.

name: light.exposure_ev
why: Per-shot exposure trim keeps a sequence matched when the generator drifts.

name: light.animate
type: enum: none | flicker | pulse | strobe | passing_lights | lightning | breathing_glow | candle | tv_wash
why: Living light stops a still-derived clip feeling like a moving photograph.
fallback: Built from flash/hot/ramp fx; complex patterns degrade to a slow pulse.

name: light.animate_rate
why: A candle flicker and a police strobe are the same effect at different rates.
fallback: Quantised to available fx keyframe intervals.

name: light.bloom
why: Highlight blooming makes anime highlights luminous rather than clipped.

name: light.god_rays
type: enum: none | subtle | strong | dusty | underwater
why: Visible light shafts are a stock anime beat deserving a first-class name.

name: light.eye_light
type: enum: none | subtle | strong | anime_sparkle | dead_flat
why: Catchlights separate a living character from a doll, and killing them reads as death or menace.

name: light.eye_shadow_bar
why: The shadow bar across the eyes is anime's standard dread and villainy device.

name: light.ambient_level
why: Overall base illumination, the difference between night and unreadable night.

name: light.haze
why: Atmospheric haze is what makes shafts, depth and distance visible at all.
fallback: Tags plus a lifted-black grade; no volumetric pass.

name: light.continuity_lock
why: Light must not re-roll between cuts in one location or the scene stops cohering.
fallback: Re-injects the scene's light tags every shot; drift is still possible.

name: grade.preset
type: enum: neutral | warm_film | cool_film | teal_orange | bleach_bypass | sepia | monochrome | high_key | low_key | faded_memory | night_blue | sodium_street | pastel_soft | vivid_pop | horror_green
why: The look variable, one word that sets an entire eq/curves stack.

name: grade.contrast
why: Direct contrast trim on top of the preset, the most-used grade adjustment.

name: grade.saturation
why: Desaturation is the fastest signal for memory, illness and drained hope.

name: grade.lift
why: Lifting blacks is the whole difference between digital video and film.

name: grade.gamma
why: Midtone weight, where a face's brightness actually lives.

name: grade.gain
why: Highlight scaling so a bright sky can be tamed without crushing the face.

name: grade.temp_shift
why: Warm/cool trim per shot keeps cuts matched when generations drift.

name: grade.tint_shift
why: Green/magenta trim is what fixes fluorescent and neon scenes.

name: grade.shadow_hue
why: Tinted shadows are the core of a designed anime palette.

name: grade.highlight_hue
why: Tinted highlights carry time of day more convincingly than midtones.

name: grade.black_point
why: Where black actually starts, which decides how deep a night reads.

name: grade.white_point
why: Ceiling control that stops whiteouts clipping into mush.

name: grade.curve
type: enum: linear | film_s | soft_s | strong_s | lifted_matte | crushed | inverted
why: The tone curve shape is the personality of a grade, above any single slider.

name: grade.halation
why: Red bleed around highlights is the signature of film-printed anime.
fallback: Approximated with a warm glow pass; not wavelength-selective.

name: grade.grain
why: A little grain unifies generated frames and hides model artefacts.

name: grade.grain_size
why: Grain size dates a film as sharply as any drawing decision.
fallback: Mapped onto available noise filter parameters; coarse and clumpy are approximate.

name: grade.sharpen
why: Video passes soften lines and a small sharpen restores anime's edge.

name: grade.lut_id
why: A single LUT is the most reliable way to match an external reference look.
fallback: Applied as a final ffmpeg lut3d when present; otherwise ignored with a warning.

name: grade.match_ref
type: string (shot id or image) or none
why: Matching one shot's grade to another is the routine fix for a mismatched cut.
fallback: Copies the reference's grade values verbatim; no histogram matching.

name: grade.animate
type: enum: none | to_warm | to_cool | to_desat | to_dark | to_bright | to_preset
why: A grade that moves during a shot is how a mood turns without a cut.
fallback: Two-segment filter chain with a linear blend; no keyframed curves.

name: grade.animate_at_pct
why: When the grade turns is the timing of the emotional beat.
fallback: Quantised to the two-segment split point.

name: grade.scope
type: enum: full_frame | exclude_characters | shadows_only | highlights_only | hue_range
why: Grading everything equally is what destroys locked character colours.
fallback: Only full_frame runs; others warn and apply full_frame with reduced strength.

name: anime.anim.on_n
why: Drawings-per-second stepping is the loudest tell that a clip is anime, and it is orthogonal to movie.fps.

name: anime.anim.step_scope
type: enum: whole_frame | content_only | character_only | fx_only | none
why: Anime steps the drawings but never the camera, so whole-frame stepping judders the pan.
fallback: content_only decimates the clip before the ffmpeg move; character_only and fx_only need plane separation and degrade to content_only with a warning.

name: anime.anim.sakuga_level
type: enum: held | limited | standard | full | showcase
why: One word allocating frame rate, motion strength, clip links, steps and retries to the cuts that deserve them.

name: anime.anim.motion_budget
type: number 0.0-1.0 (fraction of shots allowed full or showcase)
why: Anime is scheduled art, and capping fully animated cuts keeps the money on screen where it matters.
fallback: Advisory allocator that warns and demotes the lowest-priority sakuga shots; never re-renders.

name: anime.anim.hold_style
type: enum: none | held_cel | held_pan | held_partial | held_fx | pose_hold | stills_montage
why: The held cel is the backbone of limited animation and deserves a name rather than being the absence of a video pass.
fallback: held_cel, held_pan, pose_hold and stills_montage render from one keyframe with an ffmpeg move; held_partial and held_fx use a very low motion_strength i2v pass.

name: anime.anim.partial
type: list of enum: blink | mouth | eyes | hair_sway | cloth_sway | breath | flame | water | steam | smoke | leaves | rain | crowd_idle | hands
why: Animating one isolated element over a held drawing is what limited animation actually is.
fallback: Named elements are pushed into shot.motion_prompt with motion_strength clamped low; nothing guarantees only that element moves.

name: anime.anim.cycle
type: enum: none | walk | run | breathing | idle_sway | blink_loop | flag | water_loop | fire_loop | crowd_loop | sparkle_loop
why: Repeating cycles are how anime buys screen time, and a looped short clip is far cheaper than a long generation.
fallback: One LTX clip looped with a ping-pong tail; non-symmetric cycles pop at the seam.

name: anime.anim.cycle_loops
why: How many repeats decides whether a cycle reads as walking or as a stuck GIF.
fallback: Applied at edit time only; seam continuity is whatever the crossfade gives.

name: anime.anim.pose_hold_frames
why: Anime action lands by snapping to a pose and holding it; without the hold the motion reads as mush.

name: anime.anim.exaggeration
why: Squash, stretch, anticipation and overshoot are drawn-animation physics no camera or lens variable can express.
fallback: Fed to the motion prompt and camera ease overshoot; no control over the video model's deformation.

name: anime.anim.smear_style
type: enum: none | multiples | stretch | streak | ghost_trail | brush_smear | dissolve_limb
why: A drawn smear is a distortion drawing, a different thing from the post-process smear fx.
fallback: Motion-distortion tags on the mid keyframe when keyframe_mode allows one, plus the smear fx at the same percentage.

name: anime.anim.smear_frames
why: A smear lives one to three frames; longer and it becomes a blur.
fallback: Ignored; the substitute smear fx uses its own duration.

name: anime.anim.bank_id
why: Transformations, henshin and attack cut-ins are reused stock cuts, and anime reuses them on purpose.

name: anime.anim.bank_reuse
why: Whether a bank cut is the same footage or re-dressed is a look and a cost decision at once.
fallback: reuse_exact and reuse_regrade replay the cached clip through the current grade; reuse_reframe re-crops it.

name: anime.anim.cg_mix
type: enum: none | props_3d | vehicles_3d | crowd_3d | environment_3d | camera_3d | full_3dcg
why: Modern anime mixes cel-shaded 3D with 2D characters, and the mix must be declarable before it can be matched.
fallback: Requested as tags such as cel-shaded mecha; no 3D pass and no camera solve.

name: anime.draw.era
type: enum: cel_70s | cel_80s | ova_90s | early_digital_00s | modern_digital | modern_web | film_stock_retro
why: Production era bundles line, colour, artefacts and finish into the word authors think in.

name: anime.draw.line_weight
type: enum: hairline | thin | normal | thick | variable | brush | rough_genga
why: Line weight is the character-art equivalent of lens choice and is read first.

name: anime.draw.line_color
type: enum: black | dark_neutral | color_trace | per_region_trace | none
why: Coloured trace lines are a finishing decision that softens an entire film's character art.
fallback: Requested as a tag; compliance is inconsistent and there is no line pass to enforce it.

name: anime.draw.shading_steps
type: enum: flat_0 | cel_1 | cel_2 | cel_3 | soft_gradient | painterly
why: How many hard shadow steps a drawing carries is the structural difference between anime and photography.

name: anime.draw.shadow_edge
why: Cel shadow edges are hard by construction, so softening them is an explicit period decision.

name: anime.draw.shadow_hue
type: enum: darker_same_hue | blue_shift | purple_shift | complementary | warm_shift | grey_multiply
why: Anime shadow colour is chosen by a colour designer, and the hue shift is half a film's identity.
fallback: Tag plus a colorbalance shadow bias; not a per-region shadow colour.

name: anime.draw.hair_highlight
type: enum: none | soft | angel_ring | segmented | glossy | multi_band
why: The hair highlight band is a recognisable convention that dates a film to a decade.

name: anime.draw.eye_render
type: enum: moe_round | shoujo_large | shounen_bold | seinen_sharp | ova_90s | minimal_dot | realistic
why: Eye construction is house style, set once above the character list.

name: anime.draw.detail_density
type: enum: minimal | tv_standard | ova | film | ultra
why: Line count per drawing is a production tier that should inherit down a sequence.
fallback: Maps to detail tags plus a shot.steps multiplier; not a measured line count.

name: anime.draw.cel_artifacts
type: list of enum: film_grain | registration_jitter | dust_scratches | halation | telecine_wobble | paper_texture | gate_weave
why: Cel-era anime looks old because of how it was photographed, and these artefacts carry it.
fallback: Grain, dust and halation from ffmpeg noise and glow; jitter and gate weave from sub-pixel crop offsets; paper texture ignored.

name: anime.bg.style
type: enum: cel_flat | poster_color | watercolor | gouache | acrylic_matte | airbrush_soft | digital_painted | photoreal_painted | photobash | line_and_wash | ukiyo_e | graphic_flat
why: Background medium is a separate axis from finish level and is what makes a film look painted.

name: anime.bg.line
why: Whether the background carries line art signals which anime tradition a film belongs to.

name: anime.bg.style_contrast
why: The gap between character and background rendering is the defining anime image decision.
fallback: Biases the relative weight of character and background style tags in one prompt; no separate passes.

name: anime.bg.hue_relation
type: enum: matched | cooler | warmer | desaturated | higher_key | lower_key | complementary
why: Hue separation keeps a character readable against a busy painting, distinct from value separation.
fallback: Grade bias plus background colour tags; not a per-plane colour operation.

name: anime.bg.char_integration
type: enum: none | line_match | color_bleed | shared_grain | ao_contact | full_comp
why: Characters looking pasted onto the background is generated anime's most common failure.
fallback: Contact-shadow and colour-bleed tags plus a shared grain pass; no true compositing stage.

name: anime.bg.artwork_extent
why: An anime pan is performed across one oversized painting, so the art must be wider than the frame.
fallback: Renders at the largest available overscan; longer pans crop harder and lose resolution.

name: anime.bg.plate_id
why: Every cut in a location should sit on the same painting.
fallback: Locks the background seed and prompt across the scene's shots; not a literally reused plate.

name: anime.color.script
default: auto (from story.mood and story.tonality_curve per chapter)
why: The colour script is the anime colour designer's actual deliverable, not a per-shot grade preset.
fallback: Resolves into per-scene key and accent values plus grade hints; no rendered colour board.

name: anime.color.key
why: One dominant colour per scene makes a film feel designed instead of generated.

name: anime.color.accent
why: The single colour allowed to break the scheme is where the audience's eye goes.

name: anime.color.harmony
type: enum: free | analogous | complementary | split_complementary | triad | monochrome | duotone | warm_cool_split
why: Stating the palette rule lets accent, background and rim colours be derived rather than guessed.
fallback: Derives hues at author time and appends palette tags; the model can still wander.

name: anime.color.count
why: Limited palettes were a cel-era constraint authors now choose for a flat designed look.
fallback: Ignored at generation; optionally applied as a posterise pass at the grade stage.

name: anime.color.setting
type: enum: normal | night | dusk | dawn | interior_warm | fluorescent | backlit | moonlight | firelight | underwater | storm | monochrome_memory | sepia_memory | flashbulb
why: Anime approves a separate character colour set per lighting condition, before any grade.
fallback: Character colour tags plus a matching grade layer; no genuine second colour model per character.

name: anime.color.character_lock
why: A character's approved colours must survive the scene grade or recognition breaks.
fallback: Re-injects colour tags every shot and excludes them from grade extremes; drift is still possible.

name: anime.color.forbidden
why: Withholding one colour until it matters is the oldest device in a colour script.
fallback: Negative-prompt colour tags plus targeted desaturation of that hue in the grade.

name: anime.color.motif_map
why: Binding each motif to one colour makes a visual callback land without dialogue.
fallback: Injects the colour into the motif's tag bundle when present; no automatic recall.

name: anime.fx.onomatopoeia
why: Drawn sound text on screen is native anime grammar with no live-action equivalent.
fallback: Rendered with the burnt-in caption engine; needs a CJK font and cannot produce hand-drawn lettering.

name: anime.fx.onomatopoeia_style
type: enum: katakana_brush | kanji_heavy | latin_comic | hand_scrawl | glitch | none
why: Lettering style is the whole tone, separating a horror rumble from a comedy thud.
fallback: Font, weight and case substitution only; brush and scrawl degrade to a bold display face.

name: anime.fx.onomatopoeia_pos
type: enum: auto | tl | tr | bl | br | center | over_subject | diagonal
why: Where the sound word sits decides whether it reads as impact or as a caption.
fallback: Corners and centre place exactly; over_subject resolves to a static offset, not a tracked position.

name: anime.fx.technique_card
why: Naming the attack on screen is a genre staple currently faked through captions.

name: anime.fx.split_screen
type: enum: none | two_v | two_h | three_v | grid_4 | diagonal_shards | inset_pip | manga_panels | radial_wedges
why: Multi-panel frames hold three reactions at once, which frame-in-frame cannot express.
fallback: Rectangular splits composite natively; shards, wedges and manga panels degrade to the nearest rectangular layout.

name: anime.fx.deform_mode
type: enum: none | sd_chibi | head_pop | noodle_limbs | rubber_hose | mini_inset
why: Super-deformed comedy mode is an alternate character design, not an effect.

name: anime.fx.deform_scope
why: A chibi cutaway and a chibi shot are different jokes with different timing.
fallback: whole_shot and inset render; punch_in_beat becomes a short inserted shot at the chosen percentage.

name: anime.fx.face_fault
type: enum: none | jaw_drop | swirl_eyes | dot_eyes | shadowed_eyes | nosebleed | half_face_shock | crying_river | ghost_leaving
why: A comedy face fault redraws the face itself, a different channel from sticker-like emote symbols.

name: anime.fx.drawn_effect
type: enum: none | cel_fire | ink_smoke | crystal_water | geometric_debris | stylised_lightning | sparks | wind_lines | petals | glass_shatter | energy_beam
why: Effects animation is its own craft and looks nothing like photographic fire or water.
fallback: Style tags plus the nearest native fx; the effect cannot animate independently of the frame.

name: anime.fx.aura
type: enum: none | glow | flame | electric | dark_miasma | sparkle | pressure_ripple
why: A character-attached aura is a persistent drawn element held across a shot.
fallback: Aura tags plus glow fx held for the shot duration; not tracked to the body.

name: anime.fx.silhouette_mode
type: enum: none | full_silhouette | color_silhouette | strobe_silhouette | rim_only
why: Reducing a character to a flat shape is stock anime grammar for reveals and dread.

name: anime.perf.mouth_chart
why: Anime mouths run on a handful of positions, and the count separates anime from a Western cartoon.
fallback: Drives mouth tags and flap timing on still and partial paths; no viseme-accurate mouth replacement.

name: anime.perf.mouth_flap_rate
why: Flap rate makes mouth movement read as speech even when it is not phoneme-accurate.
fallback: Applied only where a mouth-only animation path exists; otherwise ignored with a warning.

name: anime.perf.mouth_sync_style
why: Japanese anime records after animation, so loose sync is correct rather than a defect.

name: anime.perf.blink_rate
why: Blinks are the cheapest sign of life in a held drawing and anime times them deliberately.
fallback: Splices a two-frame closed-eye keyframe on still and held shots; only a motion hint on i2v shots.

name: anime.perf.blink_pattern
type: enum: single | double | slow_close | held_shut | none
why: A double blink is surprise and a slow close is resignation; rate alone cannot say which.
fallback: Only single and held_shut are spliceable; the rest degrade to single with a warning.

name: anime.perf.head_tilt
why: The head tilt is anime's smallest and most-used performance beat.

name: anime.perf.pose_library
why: Named stock poses give repeatable staging without describing anatomy every time.
fallback: Expands to a pose tag bundle; no skeleton conditioning until a pose adapter exists.

name: anime.format.sequence_role
type: enum: none | avant | op | a_part | eyecatch | b_part | c_part | ed | next_preview | post_credit
default: auto (none for short; avant/a_part/b_part/ed for episode)
why: Broadcast furniture is a different axis from dramatic role and drives different music and caption rules.

name: anime.format.op_style
type: enum: none | montage | character_intro | abstract_graphic | dance | still_frames | action_showcase | typography
why: An opening is its own short film with its own grammar.
fallback: Sets pace, cut rate, transition and music defaults; shots are still authored by hand.

name: anime.format.ed_style
type: enum: none | still_pan | single_take_walk | illustration_gallery | epilogue_scene | dance | credits_over_black
why: The ending is usually the cheapest and most stylised part of an anime.
fallback: Sets shot.still, pace and transition defaults plus a credits overlay; no automatic gallery layout.

name: anime.format.eyecatch
why: The eyecatch is the act break of an anime episode and its absence is felt.

name: anime.format.eyecatch_style
type: enum: logo_card | character_pose | prop_still | chibi_gag | title_typography | silhouette_card
why: The eyecatch is a tiny authored image that tells the audience what kind of show this is.

name: anime.format.next_preview
type: enum: none | clips_vo | still_vo | tease_only | gag
why: The next-episode preview is a fixed anime form with its own voice and pacing rules.
fallback: Assembles from marked shots with a VO track; no automatic clip selection.

name: anime.format.episode_no
why: Episode numbering drives titles, previews and file naming for a series.

name: anime.format.broadcast_safe
why: Strobe and flash limits exist because broadcast anime injured viewers once.
fallback: Caps flash frequency and fx intensity at author time; no photosensitivity analysis.

name: audio.music.cue
why: The music variable, naming which cue plays so it can start, stop and recur.

name: audio.music.prompt
default: auto (from genre, mood, tone and intensity)
why: The generator takes text, so the resolved prompt must be an authorable field.

name: audio.music.genre
type: enum: none | orchestral | piano_solo | strings | ambient | synth | city_pop | jazz | rock | metal | electronic | lofi | choral | folk | traditional_ja | chiptune | drone
why: Genre is the fastest handle on a score and seeds instrumentation and tempo.

name: audio.music.instrumentation
why: Naming the instruments is what stops every generated cue sounding the same.

name: audio.music.tempo_bpm
why: Tempo is the link between music and cut rate and must be statable.
fallback: Passed as a prompt hint; the generator does not guarantee the tempo.

name: audio.music.key
type: enum: auto | c | d | e | f | g | a | b (with sharps/flats)
why: A stated key lets reprises and stingers actually match the main theme.
fallback: Prompt hint only; no key extraction or enforcement.

name: audio.music.mode
type: enum: major | minor | modal | atonal | pentatonic | whole_tone
why: Mode carries emotional valence more reliably than any adjective in the prompt.
fallback: Prompt hint only.

name: audio.music.intensity
why: One dial for how loud and busy the score is, independent of what it plays.

name: audio.music.role
type: enum: none | score | source | diegetic | anthem | theme | underscore | sting | silence_bed
why: Whether music exists in the world changes mixing, filtering and perspective.

name: audio.music.motif
why: A named musical theme is how a film's emotional callbacks are built.
fallback: Re-uses the motif's cached cue or its prompt seed; no melodic continuity guarantee.

name: audio.music.reprise_of
why: A reprise must point at the earlier cue rather than be re-described from scratch.
fallback: Re-renders from the original prompt with the same seed; not the same recording.

name: audio.music.start_at_pct
why: Where music enters within a scene is a directing choice, not a technical one.

name: audio.music.length_s
why: Generated cues need a target length or they must be crudely cut.

name: audio.music.transition
type: enum: cut | crossfade | fade_in | fade_out | hard_stop | stinger | build | drop | tempo_shift | key_change | reprise | bridge | overlap_hold | silence_into
why: The music-transition variable the author asked for, naming how one cue becomes the next.
fallback: cut, crossfade, fades, hard_stop and overlap_hold render exactly; build, drop, tempo_shift and key_change become two cues joined by a crossfade with a warning.

name: audio.music.transition_s
why: Music transition length is the difference between a stumble and a turn.

name: audio.music.transition_at
type: enum: on_cut | on_scene_start | on_scene_end | at_pct | on_beat | on_line_end
why: Where the change lands is what makes it feel scored rather than accidental.
fallback: on_beat resolves to the nearest authored time; no beat detection.

name: audio.music.build_s
why: A build before a climax is a scored event with its own duration.
fallback: Approximated by a rising gain ramp on the outgoing cue.

name: audio.music.stinger
type: enum: none | hit | riser | reverse_swell | dread_low | comedy_slide | choir_hit | taiko_hit
why: A single musical hit on a cut is the most-used scoring device in anime.
fallback: Generated as a short Stable Audio one-shot and mixed at the cut; not key-matched to the score.

name: audio.music.loop
why: Looping a short cue is how a long scene gets scored cheaply.
fallback: Looped with a crossfade; seams are audible on non-symmetric cues.

name: audio.music.duck_db
why: How far music drops under dialogue is the most consequential mix number.

name: audio.music.seed
why: Reproducible music matters as much as reproducible images.

name: audio.sfx.list
why: The sound-effects variable, placing named one-shots inside a shot.

name: audio.sfx.prompt
why: Generated SFX need text, so the derived prompt must be overridable.

name: audio.sfx.category
type: enum: none | foley | impact | whoosh | ui | nature | mechanical | magic | vocal_nonverbal | destruction | vehicle
why: Category selects generation settings, EQ and default level in one word.

name: audio.sfx.auto_foley
why: Footsteps and cloth should appear from blocking rather than be authored per shot.
fallback: Generates from movement and ground_state at a fixed level; no timing to the picture.

name: audio.sfx.impact_sync
why: An impact effect must land on the same frame as the impact flash.

name: audio.sfx.transition_whoosh
type: enum: none | auto | soft | hard | reverse | doppler
why: Whip pans and smash cuts are half sound, and the sound is what sells them.

name: audio.sfx.tail_s
why: Sound that continues past the cut is what binds two shots together.

name: audio.sfx.pan
why: Placing a sound off-centre is free depth and follows screen direction.

name: audio.sfx.gain_db
why: A default effects level so nothing needs mixing to be audible.

name: audio.sfx.reverb_send
why: Effects must sit in the same room as the dialogue or the scene splits apart.
fallback: Fixed room presets per space type; no impulse-response matching.

name: audio.amb.bed
why: The continuous ambience bed is what makes cuts inside one location feel continuous.

name: audio.amb.layers
why: Ambience is built from stacked layers, not a single generated file.
fallback: Rendered as a small number of looped generated beds mixed together.

name: audio.amb.level_db
why: Ambience level is the floor everything else is judged against.

name: audio.amb.continuity
why: Ambience that restarts every cut is the loudest sign of machine assembly.

name: audio.amb.room_tone
type: enum: none | small_room | large_room | hall | corridor | classroom | street | forest | cave | vehicle | underwater
why: Room tone is what makes silence sound like a place rather than a missing file.

name: audio.amb.weather_sound
type: enum: auto | none | rain_light | rain_heavy | thunder | wind | snow_muffle | storm
why: Weather is heard more than seen and should follow the weather variable automatically.

name: audio.mix.target_lufs
why: One loudness target so the whole film normalises consistently.

name: audio.mix.true_peak_db
why: Peak ceiling that keeps the master from clipping on delivery.

name: audio.mix.dialogue_db
why: Dialogue is the anchor every other element is set relative to.

name: audio.mix.music_db
why: A stated music level stops every scene needing a manual balance.

name: audio.mix.duck_mode
why: How music gets out of the way of dialogue is a policy, not a per-cue fix.
fallback: Static gain reduction over dialogue regions when sidechain analysis is unavailable.

name: audio.mix.dynamics
type: enum: wide | cinematic | broadcast | compressed | loud
why: Dynamic range policy decides whether quiet scenes stay quiet.

name: audio.mix.stereo_width
why: Width is a mood tool: narrow for claustrophobia, wide for scale.

name: audio.mix.perspective
type: enum: objective | subject_pov | distant | muffled | underwater | tinnitus | inside_head
why: Sound perspective is how a subjective POV is actually communicated.
fallback: Built from lowpass, reverb and level presets; no true binaural modelling.

name: audio.mix.silence
type: enum: none | soft | full | absolute | pre_impact | after_shock
why: The silence variable, a deliberate dropout that is one of the strongest audio devices.

name: audio.mix.silence_s
why: How long the silence holds is the whole effect.

name: audio.mix.fade_in_s
why: Audio needs its own fade separate from picture at structural boundaries.

name: audio.mix.fade_out_s
why: An audio tail after picture ends is how a chapter releases.

name: audio.vo.mode
type: enum: none | narration | inner_monologue | letter | phone | radio | announcement | memory_echo
why: Voice-over is processed and mixed differently from in-scene dialogue.

name: audio.vo.char
why: Whose inner voice we hear must be explicit or the POV blurs.

name: audio.vo.processing
type: enum: dry | close_intimate | reverb_wash | telephone | radio | distant | doubled | whisper_layer
why: Processing is what tells the audience a voice is interior rather than spoken.

name: dialogue.lines
why: The dialogue variable, holding what is actually said in this shot.

name: dialogue.line.speaker
why: Every line needs an owner so voice, emotion and mouth follow the right body.

name: dialogue.line.text
why: The spoken text itself, feeding TTS, captions and flap timing.

name: dialogue.line.delivery
type: enum: neutral | soft | warm | flat | clipped | urgent | shouted | whispered | trembling | laughing | crying | breathless | sarcastic | tender | cold
why: How a line is said is the acting, and it is separable from the emotion word.
fallback: Mapped to emotion vectors on engines that support them; others get rate and pitch changes only.

name: dialogue.line.emotion
type: enum: inherit | plus any char.emotion value
why: A line can carry a different feeling from the face, and that gap is the drama.
fallback: Only engines with emotion vectors honour this; others fall back to delivery presets.

name: dialogue.line.emotion_strength
why: Emotion vectors need a magnitude or every line is maximally acted.
fallback: Clamped to whatever range the selected engine exposes.

name: dialogue.line.volume
type: enum: whisper | quiet | normal | raised | shout | scream
why: Volume changes both the performance and the mix, so it must be one field.

name: dialogue.line.rate
why: Speaking rate is character, and it also decides whether the line fits the shot.

name: dialogue.line.pitch_shift
why: Small pitch moves cover age, stress and non-human characters cheaply.

name: dialogue.line.at_pct
why: Where a line starts inside the shot is timing, and timing is comedy and tension.

name: dialogue.line.pause_before_s
why: The beat before a line is often the performance.

name: dialogue.line.pause_after_s
why: Trailing air decides whether a line lands or is stepped on.

name: dialogue.line.overlap
why: Overlapping speech is how arguments and crowds sound real.

name: dialogue.line.offscreen
type: enum: on_screen | off_screen | back_to_camera | behind_door | over_phone
why: Off-screen lines need different mixing and no mouth animation at all.

name: dialogue.line.processing
type: enum: none | phone | radio | pa | tv | muffled | reverb | underwater | distorted
why: Source colouring on a line is often the entire storytelling point.

name: dialogue.line.language
type: enum: inherit | en | ja | zh | ko | es | fr | de | other
why: A single foreign line is common and needs its own voice and caption handling.

name: dialogue.line.subtitle
why: Subtitle text often differs from spoken text, especially across languages.

name: dialogue.turn_gap_s
why: The gap between speakers is the rhythm of a conversation.

name: dialogue.style
type: enum: naturalistic | formal | archaic | slangy | terse | florid | childlike | military | keigo | rough
why: Speech register belongs above the line so a whole character or scene inherits it.

name: dialogue.lipsync
type: enum: none | flap | loose | tight | closed
why: The lipsync variable, stating how hard mouth movement must match audio.
fallback: loose and flap drive mouth tags and timed mouth keyframes; tight warns and behaves as loose.

name: dialogue.voice.engine
type: enum: auto | engine_a | engine_b | engine_emotion | engine_ja
why: Engines differ in language and emotion support, so the choice must be authorable.

name: dialogue.voice.id
why: A stable voice per character is as important as a stable face.

name: dialogue.voice.timbre
type: enum: bright | warm | dark | breathy | nasal | rough | clear | childlike | aged
why: Timbre is casting, and casting is not something to leave to a default seed.
fallback: Selects the nearest available voice in the pool; no timbre synthesis.

name: dialogue.voice.accent
why: Accent and dialect are character facts that must persist across every scene.
fallback: Prompt or voice-pool selection only; unavailable accents warn and use the base voice.

name: caption.mode
type: enum: none | dialogue | full | forced_only | signs_only | karaoke
why: The captions variable, deciding what text is burnt into the picture.

name: caption.language
type: enum: inherit | en | ja | zh | ko | es | fr | de
why: Caption language is separate from spoken language for subtitled films.

name: caption.font
why: Font choice is both legibility and tone, and CJK needs a specific face.

name: caption.size_pct
why: Caption size must scale with canvas rather than be a fixed pixel value.

name: caption.position
type: enum: bottom | top | bottom_left | bottom_right | center | under_speaker
why: Captions sometimes have to move to avoid the composition.
fallback: Fixed positions place exactly; under_speaker uses a static offset from framing, not tracking.

name: caption.style
type: enum: plain_white | outlined | boxed | drop_shadow | anime_yellow | soft_grey
why: Caption styling is what keeps text readable over a bright anime frame.

name: caption.max_chars
why: Line length is the main readability control for burnt-in text.

name: caption.max_lines
why: More than two lines covers the picture and stops being a caption.

name: caption.reading_speed
why: Minimum on-screen time so captions can actually be read.

name: caption.speaker_labels
why: Off-screen and crowded scenes need attribution the audience can follow.

name: caption.sfx_captions
why: Accessibility captions for sound are a distinct output from dialogue subtitles.
fallback: Emitted from named SFX ids only; generated effects have no descriptions.

name: caption.offset_s
why: Global timing trim when TTS and caption timings drift apart.

name: caption.signs_policy
why: On-screen signage in another language needs a stated handling policy.
fallback: Renders as an extra caption line; no positioned sign replacement.

name: render.sampler
why: Sampler choice changes line quality noticeably on anime checkpoints.

name: render.scheduler
why: Scheduler pairs with sampler and belongs beside it as an inheritable default.

name: render.overscan_pct
why: Extra rendered margin is what makes post pans, crops and shakes possible without softening.

name: render.upscale
why: Hero shots deserve resolution that filler shots would waste.

name: render.face_detailer
why: Faces at small scale are where anime generation fails most visibly.

name: render.i2v_steps
why: The video pass has its own quality/time trade separate from the keyframe.

name: render.i2v_cfg
why: Motion adherence versus stability is a distinct dial from image CFG.

name: render.frame_interp
why: Interpolation is how a low-fps generation reaches delivery fps, and it fights anime stepping.
fallback: Applied after stepping so held drawings survive; smooth mode can reintroduce video feel.

name: render.color_space
why: A stated colour space keeps grades consistent between preview and delivery.

name: render.codec
type: enum: h264 | h265 | prores | vp9 | av1
why: Delivery codec decides compatibility and how much the grade survives.

name: render.bitrate
why: Flat anime colour banding is a bitrate problem before it is an art problem.

name: render.proxy_mode
why: Fast low-resolution passes are how an author iterates on structure before committing.

name: render.cache_policy
why: Re-rendering unchanged shots is the single largest waste in an iterative film.

name: render.order
why: Render order decides how soon an author sees the shots that matter.
fallback: sequential and hero_first are implemented; others fall back to sequential.

name: render.on_fail
why: A failed shot in a long render must not silently produce a broken film.

name: render.placeholder
why: What stands in for a failed shot decides whether a rough cut is still watchable.

name: render.version_tag
why: Versioned outputs are how an author compares two cuts instead of overwriting one.

name: render.watermark
why: Draft marking prevents a work-in-progress cut being mistaken for the final film.
